clue.text: Reduce length of a card game

parts.note: bridge is a trick-taking card game for four players

explanation.surface: Someone shortening a game of cards to save time.
explanation.definitionFit: To abridge a text is to shorten it, cutting its overall size while keeping the sense.

clue.text: Expert, one in a suit

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a highly skilled person
second meaning: the card counting one in each suit of a pack

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests an expert in business dress; the suit is a suit of playing cards.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means a top performer and also the single-pip playing card found in every suit.

clue.text: Describing oneself maybe as fixer, lever mostly repaired

indicators.note: something repaired has been put back together differently, so these letters are rearranged
mostly means most of the word lever, its final letter dropped

explanation.surface: An odd mix of a handyman's fixer and a lever being mended.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' cuts lever to LEVE; 'repaired' rearranges FIXER plus LEVE.
explanation.definitionFit: In grammar a reflexive pronoun such as oneself refers back to the subject of the verb.

clue.text: Prune weed

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to cut short or trim
second meaning: a broad-leaved wild plant

explanation.walkthrough: Both words look like gardening instructions or a fruit; they are two separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: Dock means to cut back, as with a tail or wages, and is also a common coarse plant gardeners pull up.

clue.text: Stand shaking under bottom of gable

indicators.note: shaking jumbles things up, so the letters of under are rearranged
in a down clue the bottom of a word is its last letter, here of gable

explanation.surface: Someone standing trembling beneath the low end of a gable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shaking' turns UNDER into ENDUR; 'bottom of' gives the E ending gable.
explanation.definitionFit: To stand something is to tolerate or put up with it, which is what endure means.

clue.text: Arrive shortly to seize doctor's computer drive

indicators.note: to seize is to grab and hold, so one piece is held inside the other
shortly means the word is cut short, losing its final letter

parts.note: to arrive is to come
DR is the standard abbreviation for doctor

explanation.surface: Someone arriving to grab the doctor's computer drive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shortly' cuts COME to COM, which then holds DR.
explanation.definitionFit: A CD-ROM is a read-only compact disc used for storing data, loosely a computer drive or its disc.

clue.text: Lifting some cracked rib, eg accounts for pet budgie, say

indicators.note: in a down clue lifting raises the letters up, so they read in reverse
some means only part of these words is used, the letters sitting inside them

parts.note: the run of letters straddles these words

explanation.surface: Lifting accounts with a cracked rib, oddly tied to a pet bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some' finds DRIBEGAC inside cracked rib, eg accounts; 'Lifting' turns it upward.
explanation.definitionFit: A budgerigar is a typical example of a small bird kept in a cage as a household pet.

clue.text: City having foremost of roles in Olympics

indicators.note: foremost means front, so the first letter of each following word is taken

explanation.surface: A city given leading roles at the Olympic Games.
explanation.walkthrough: Rio de Janeiro hosted the 2016 Olympics, so the surface fits the answer too.
explanation.definitionFit: Rio de Janeiro is a major Brazilian metropolis, commonly shortened to Rio.

clue.text: Riots most awkward for people in cars

indicators.note: awkward suggests something clumsy and out of order, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Riots are most awkward for those caught in traffic.
explanation.definitionFit: Motorists are drivers of motor vehicles, people travelling by automobile.

clue.text: Erased last trace of coffee, with decaff sent back

indicators.note: the last trace of a word is its final letter, here of coffee
sent back means the word decaff is written in reverse

explanation.surface: Someone wiping away coffee stains after returning a decaf.
explanation.walkthrough: E from coffee, then 'sent back' gives FFACED from decaff.
explanation.definitionFit: To efface is to rub out or wipe away, so effaced is a synonym for removed.

clue.text: Spirit provided by good entertainer

parts.note: a host entertains guests

explanation.surface: Spirits supplied by a generous party-giver.
explanation.definitionFit: A ghost is the spectre of a dead person, a spirit in the supernatural sense.

clue.text: Swiss painter king sheltered

parts.note: K is the chess and card abbreviation for king
lee describes the side away from the wind, the sheltered side

explanation.surface: A Swiss artist who gave refuge to a monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: Paul Klee was a Swiss-born German artist famous for his colourful abstract pictures.

clue.text: Girl and daughter in football team in Himalayan city

parts.note: Kath is a girl's name, short for Katherine

indicators.note: in places the daughter inside the football team

parts.note: Man U is the nickname of Manchester United, an English football club
D is the genealogical abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: A girl and her daughter supporting a football club from the Himalayas.
explanation.definitionFit: Kathmandu is the capital of Nepal, lying in a valley among the Himalaya mountains.

clue.text: More unwholesome food in front of funeral platform

indicators.note: in front of places the food word before the platform word

parts.note: grub is informal slang for food
a bier is the stand on which a coffin rests

explanation.surface: Unhealthy snacks laid out before a coffin stand at a wake.
explanation.definitionFit: Grubby means dirty or sordid, so grubbier is the comparative for something less clean.

clue.text: Not up to it — except when wearing headgear?

definitions.text: Not up to it — except when wearing headgear?

parts.words: Not up to it — except when wearing headgear?
parts.note: someone able only while in a cap is otherwise unable

explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as three words, IN CAP ABLE: fit for the task only when wearing a cap.
explanation.definitionFit: Incapable means lacking the ability to do something, unfit for a task.

clue.text: Exotic agora: one place you can't enter

indicators.note: exotic means strange and foreign, so these letters take an unfamiliar new arrangement

explanation.surface: An exotic Greek marketplace that visitors are barred from.
explanation.walkthrough: An agora was a public square in ancient Greece.
explanation.definitionFit: A no-go area is a district where entry is forbidden or too dangerous to visit.

clue.text: Stand round day after journey

indicators.note: after places the round and day letters following the journey word

parts.note: a trip is a journey
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: Instructions to stand around for a day after a long trip.
explanation.definitionFit: A tripod is a three-legged support for a camera or telescope, a kind of stand.

clue.text: Bloomer, feeding caribou's tail to dangerous reptiles

indicators.note: feeding one thing to another puts it inside, here into the reptiles

parts.note: crocs is short for crocodiles

indicators.note: the tail of a word is its final letter, here of caribou

parts.note: the word caribou, whose tail is wanted

explanation.surface: A grisly blunder: feeding a reindeer's tail to crocodiles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bloomer' looks like a mistake; it means a flowering plant.
explanation.definitionFit: A crocus is a small spring flower, and a bloomer is crossword language for anything that blooms.

clue.text: Shame about Grammar School being such a dirty place!

indicators.note: about means around, so the pity word goes round the school letters

parts.note: what a shame and what a pity mean the same

explanation.surface: A lament that a grammar school has become filthy.
explanation.definitionFit: A pigsty, where pigs are kept, is proverbially filthy; any messy room gets called one.

clue.text: It helps to remember conmen I'm messing around

indicators.note: messing around suggests disorder, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A memory aid, offered by tricksters fooling about.
explanation.definitionFit: A mnemonic is a rhyme or device that assists memory, such as a phrase whose initials encode a list.

clue.text: Work required in shop, usually

indicators.note: required in means found within these words, the letters spanning the gap

explanation.surface: A job that usually has to be done in the shop.
explanation.definitionFit: An opus is a musical or artistic composition, a creative work.

clue.text: Minor carpeting upset university teacher

indicators.note: in a down clue upset turns the letters upside down, so they read in reverse

parts.note: a rug is a small piece of carpet

explanation.surface: A lecturer upset by a scrappy bit of carpet.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'upset' is a natural signal to read upward; 'Minor carpeting' means a small carpet, not a junior official.
explanation.definitionFit: A guru is a spiritual guide in Hinduism, and more broadly any revered mentor.

clue.text: Back Rex, for example, in African country

indicators.note: back means the letters are read backwards

parts.note: Rex, like Reg, is a short form of Reginald

explanation.surface: Supporting Rex, maybe a dog, somewhere in Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: Rex is an example of a pet form of Reginald (the actor Rex Harrison was born Reginald), so REG; 'Back' reverses REGIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Niger is a landlocked West African nation named after the river that crosses it.

clue.text: Antelope never used to be picked up?

indicators.note: picked up means heard, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: something new has never been used

explanation.surface: An antelope too pristine ever to be lifted.
explanation.definitionFit: The gnu, or wildebeest, is a large African grazing animal of the antelope family.

clue.text: Bust by Laurens, initially awfully rough around the chin?

indicators.note: awfully suggests a bad mess, so these letters are reworked
initially means the first letter of Laurens is taken

explanation.surface: A sculpted head by Laurens with a crudely bristly jaw.
explanation.walkthrough: Henri Laurens was a French sculptor. 'initially' gives L, and 'awfully' rearranges BUSTBY with L.
explanation.definitionFit: Stubbly describes a chin with short unshaven bristles, rough to the touch.

clue.text: Foreign money you no longer earn, finally

parts.note: ye is an old form of you, no longer in use

indicators.note: finally means the last letter of earn

explanation.surface: Overseas cash that you no longer earn.
explanation.definitionFit: The yen is the currency of Japan, so to a British solver a foreign unit of money.

clue.text: Suave UCL man periodically appearing in a flap

indicators.note: periodically means at regular intervals, so every other letter is taken

explanation.surface: A smooth London college man turning up in a panic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a flap' looks like a state of panic, but the definition is the fleshy flap; UCL is University College London.
explanation.definitionFit: The uvula is the small fleshy lobe hanging at the back of the soft palate.

clue.text: Yankee with no euro to change? I accept the terms!

parts.note: Yankee is Y in the NATO phonetic alphabet

indicators.note: to change means the letters of no euro are rearranged

explanation.surface: An American without euros needing currency exchange agrees a deal.
explanation.definitionFit: You're on is an idiom accepting a bet or challenge, agreeing to the proposed conditions.
